subject.title: [Bug] Missing Expiration Grace Window/Threshold in Token Credential Validation

question: Should non-refreshable token profiles remain usable until exact expiry, or should OpenClaw reject them early under a defined minimum remaining-lifetime policy?
rationale: Current code and canonical documentation deliberately distinguish plain token eligibility from refreshable OAuth timing, so early rejection changes a cross-path authentication and fallback contract.

options.title: Keep Exact Expiry
options.body: Retain the current contract and use refreshable OAuth credentials when uninterrupted long-running operations require proactive refresh.

options.title: Add Shared Margin
options.body: Define one global early-expiry rule and update every credential consumer, diagnostic surface, fallback path, test, and document consistently.

options.title: Use Provider Policy
options.body: Allow provider-owned auth behavior to request a minimum remaining lifetime only where its token semantics justify early rejection.

recommendation.title: Keep Exact Expiry
recommendation.body: Retain the current contract and use refreshable OAuth credentials when uninterrupted long-running operations require proactive refresh.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the cited discovery-expiry behavior and have the strongest history across the affected auth resolution surfaces.
